scene1Childhood.memory: My mother taught me to knead bread in our small kitchen. I got flour on my nose.

scene2TeenFreedom.memory: I took the bus to my first bakery job, carrying the apron she had sewn.

scene3LeapOfFaith.memory: When the bakery closed, I started baking for neighbors at home.

scene4Romance.memory: Your grandpa carried the heavy bread baskets. He always sneaked one warm roll.

scene5LegacyFinale.memory: Leo, I want you to remember our Sunday bread. Making something for someone is a way to say I love you.

beats.narration: Leo, my mother taught me to knead bread in our small kitchen. I got flour on my nose. Those are the hands and the kitchen I remember.
beats.emotionalPurpose: Invite Leo into a concrete childhood memory of learning and care.

beats.narration: Later, I took the bus to my first bakery job. I carried the apron my mother had sewn. Something from our kitchen came along with me.
beats.emotionalPurpose: Connect a step into independence with the care carried from home.

beats.narration: When the bakery closed, I began baking for neighbors at home. Your grandpa carried the heavy bread baskets, and always sneaked one warm roll. That was our team.
beats.emotionalPurpose: Turn a setback into mutual care with a warm, source-grounded comic detail.

beats.narration: Leo, I want you to remember our Sunday bread. Making something for someone is a way to say I love you. That is the memory I want you to keep.
beats.emotionalPurpose: Pass the explicit source message of love directly from grandmother to grandson.
